subject: Microburst latency spike — triage & customer messaging
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, ops@checkoutly.com
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 01 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: [ALERT] Microburst: p95/p99 latency spike 09:08-09:28 PT — Checkoutly impact

Team,

We just observed a microburst between 09:08 and 09:28 PT affecting Checkoutly's gen-api routes (model: rw-large-v1). Key points:
- P95 jumped from ~220ms → ~1.8s, p99 ~2.9s.
- Affected shards show rapid KV-cache misses and queueing on A100 pool 3.
- Autoscaler initiated scale-up but instances came up with cold KV loads — saw sequential warm-ups that didn't keep up.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Rate-limited Checkoutly route by 30% at 09:15 to blunt throughput.
- Applied sticky routing to route a subset to dedicated pool 1 at 09:20.

Attached: timeline.csv (token-level timeline + ingress rates).

Ask: can product/comms help draft a short, honest customer note (ops@checkoutly.com included) while eng/SRE triage root cause? Also need decision on whether we proactively roll back the canary we deployed to the gen-runtime yesterday night.

Ben
Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@checkoutly.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Mar 2028 09:22:17 -0800
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Microburst: p95/p99 latency spike 09:08-09:28 PT — Checkoutly impact

Thanks for the heads up. We did see a spike in customer-reported errors around 09:10 — checkout flow timeouts. Our telemetry shows a surge of validation calls from a new A/B test that rolled out at 09:05 and targeted 25% of traffic. Ops dashboard: https://status.checkoutly.com/incident/3241

Questions:
- ETA for stabilization?
- Will this be a sustained problem for the next few hours (we have a marketing push at 11:00 PT)?

Appreciate a clear statement we can share with our on-call and support teams.

— Alice
Alice Nguyen
TPM, Checkoutly

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@checkoutly.com, alice.nguyen@checkoutly.com
Date: Tue, 01 Mar 2028 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Draft: short customer update + product/roadmap asks — please review

Team — drafting a one-paragraph update for Checkoutly and want quick engineering confirmation on the cause and next steps. Draft below (feel free to edit inline):

"Checkoutly — we observed a short-lived latency spike affecting validation calls between 09:08–09:28 PT. Our operations team applied rate-limiting and traffic rerouting to reduce impact; engineering is investigating and plans a targeted rollback of a runtime canary that may have increased cold-cache miss rates. We will follow up with a root cause and timeline for remediation in the next 4 hours."

Product/roadmap asks for eng: if this is indeed a canary-induced KV warmup ordering issue, we should evaluate a pre-warm step in the rollout flow and add a checkbox to the runtime canary template. Also want to know if we need a short-term config flag to prioritize warm-up for enterprise routes (Checkoutly).

Attachments: I have a heap dump request coming from Ben — ben, please attach if relevant (ffwd-heapdump.tar.gz).

Please reply with: 1) confirm cause (canary vs autoscaler vs other), 2) immediate fix we will do now, 3) what product/roadmap change we ask the PM to prioritise.

Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@checkoutly.com, alice.nguyen@checkoutly.com
Date: Tue, 01 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft: short customer update + product/roadmap asks — please review

Quick triage notes — from infra/eng: 
- Correlation looks strong with last night's runtime canary (canary id: canary-20280229-09). Canary adjusted kernel scheduling and preemption timeout; observed that new instances were brought up without warmed KV and the scheduling change increased tail access latency during warm-ups.
- Autoscaler behaved as expected but couldn't hide the cold-start tail because the canary reduced effective concurrency on warm instances.

Immediate plan (we can execute in the next 30–60m):
1) Roll back canary (started rollback at 10:02).
2) Increase pro-warm concurrency on dedicated pool 1 for Checkoutly for 30 minutes.
3) Add a short-lived routing rule to avoid re-routing heavy validation traffic to recently rolled instances.

Roadmap asks (for PM/Runtime):
- Add a "pre-warm" stage to canary rollouts where KV caches are seeded before traffic ramp.
- Make an enterprise flag to pin critical routes to warmed pools during rollouts.
- Instrumentation: emit per-canary warm-up success metric and alert if <95% warmed after X minutes.

I'll attach the quick kernel scheduling diffs and file an INF ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4721

Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Runtime

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@checkoutly.com>, ops@checkoutly.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Mar 2028 14:45:00 -0800
Subject: Checkoutly — incident update and next steps (short)

Alice / Checkoutly ops —

Thank you for the quick signal and patience. Summary and actions: 

What happened (short): between 09:08–09:28 PT we saw a spike in validation call latency tied to a runtime canary that changed kernel scheduling behavior and increased cold-KV miss tail latency during instance warm-up. A simultaneous A/B test from your side increased validation traffic at ~09:05 which amplified impact.

What we did:
- Rolled back the canary at ~10:02 and bumped pro-warm concurrency on the dedicated pool serving your routes.
- Applied temporary routing to avoid recently-warmed instances.
- Restored p95/p99 to baseline by ~10:18.

Impact: short-lived timeouts for a subset of traffic during the 09:08–09:28 window. Based on our metrics and your reports, the majority of sessions recovered without requiring retries.

Next steps:
- Internal: INF-4721 opened to add a pre-warm stage and a warm-up health metric; we'll share the ticket ETA and product timeline by EOD tomorrow.
- Offering: we will review the incident in postmortem and propose a goodwill credit for affected calls.

We are sorry for the interruption. If you need a synchronous readout before your 11:00 PT push, we can stand up a 20-minute bridge at 10:30 PT — please let us know.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.docx (internal draft).

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
